# spw.quest

> Spw is a notation for a reading you can compare: a mark says what a word is doing, and a brace says which slot it fills. An answer written in Spw can be parsed, compared, and opened as a card or a canvas.

An address and a line together, as in "spw.quest rpgwednesday<card>", ask for an answer written in Spw. The line names the subject and its <concept> names the kind of answer. An answer is plain Spw text, with no code fence and no sentence before it. A person setting up a repository wants [the recipe](https://spw.quest/init) instead.

Containers ([], {}, (), <>) are independent boundaries, not a fixed template. word[mode]{body}(scene)<concept> is one shorthand; containers may stand alone (?["question"], (rehearsal), {a, b}), reorder ((live)stream{a, b}), nest (cut{[rough] ~> [locked]}), or lead with a mark (!ship{page}). Include only meaningful containers.

- word: optional subject (or Persona@subject).
- [mode]: stance, lens, or schema key.
- {body}: parts inside (dot = one name, comma = company, semicolon = order, ~> = path).
- (scene): where or when it stands.
- <concept>: kind or outward channel.

A mark goes right before a word, with no space after it:

- ~ potential: Keep a path open without taking it.
- ? wonder: Open a question you can close again.
- ! action: Commit a move so its consequence can be seen.
- * value: Mark what carries weight here.
- . ground: Come back to the local default.
- ^ ascension: Lift parts into one relation you can inspect.
- # vibration: Name a structure so it can be found again.
- @ perspective: Say who is looking, and from where.
- & subject: Name what the relation is about.
- = configuration: Keep this here, under this name.
- % measure: Compare, weigh, or level the field.
- $ substrate: Name what carries the charge: time, money, memory, attention.

Quoted text takes double quotes. Four particles sit on the # plane and ~ aspect axis: #>name (deixis) points forward to a file or block, #:kind (case) classifies its layer or role, #!intent (mood) marks active intent or stance, and ~#aspect (aspect) marks deferred expectation or reading (~#expect: "...", ~#lens(comparison)).

Unquoted words in brackets (^seed[Session], #[episode], ~[scene]) key structured schema frames with no spaces and field: "value" slots. Quoted text in brackets (^seed["porch notes"]) or scopes (^"section", ?["question?"]) holds free titles or prose without claiming a fixed template key. Perspective holders put @ after the name so the contents of that perspective follow (Persona@[mode]{...}, viewer@subject), while file-handle aliases declare @alias: ~"./file.spw#name". Top-level bindings use name = "value"; leading marks hug their word, joins between two lines (a ~ b, a ^ b, a @ b) take spaces, >>[date] tag — note opens a stream entry, and ~"./file.spw#name" cites another surface.

A word<card> is the line with its [mode], {body} and (scene) filled in from what is known, then a seed card, and a seed card always names its schema template. Known templates on spwashi.com (Session, Wonder.Prompt, NewYear.Joy, Services.Offer, Folio.Order, Ask.Card, Costuming.Way) open directly into cards when pasted. ^seed[Session] has fields date, scene, turn, carry and revisit (unknown fields omitted). Asked garden<card>, this is an answer:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost, seedlings}(saturday)<card>
    ^seed[Session]{
      scene: "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"
      carry: "the beds planted last week"
      revisit: "what survived the frost?"
    }

For a word you know nothing about, not knowing is the card. ^seed[Wonder.Prompt] has the fields question, tension, material, relay and revisit, and each says what would have to be found out:

    nightmarket<card>
    ^seed[Wonder.Prompt]{
      question: "what is nightmarket, and who keeps it?"
      tension: "the name is all that was given"
      relay: "whoever named it"
      revisit: "once a page says what it is"
    }

For a free-form heading instead of a template card, quote the title in brackets:

    ^seed["porch notes"]{
      #>opening
      #:notes #!draft
      ~#expect: "keep what changes when one slot turns"
    }

A word<question> is the question, what is expected, and the probe that would answer it:

    ?["Will the seedlings survive a frost?"]{
      ~#expect: "the covered bed holds and the open bed does not"
      !probe{ "read both beds the morning after the first frost" }
    }

A word<change> says what happened, what changed, and how it was checked:

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ the open bed lost its seedlings to a frost }
      ![change]{ every bed is covered before dusk in November }
      *[verify]{ all four beds came through the next frost }
    }

Any other <concept> is the line with its slots filled and one plain sentence:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost}(saturday)<plot>
    *says = "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"

Facts about a word come from the Card address below, which lists what the site holds for it. When revising a line for meaning or logic, edit inside its word, [mode], {body}, or (scene) while keeping its marks and braces intact so the parse tree holds. Lines travel across peer surfaces: paste on spwashi.com (opens known seeds as cards or inspects AST at /tools/spw-parser/), lay out spatially on factshift.center (?spw= line, #spw64= script), or compose material specs on texture.website (/{material}.spw). On X an answer fits 280 characters and has no @ directly before a name, since that notifies the account; a # before a letter shows as a tag. A link to https://spw.quest/card?line= with the line percent-encoded unfurls as a link card.

## Addresses

Every address below answers with a page that reads with no script, except Canvas.

- [Card](https://spw.quest/card.txt?line=rpgwednesday%3Ccard%3E): You hold a line and want what the site holds for its word before answering it, as text. line: one line, 200 characters. /card with the same line is a small page that unfurls as a link card, and spw.quest/ followed by the line itself answers the same. Example: line = rpgwednesday<card>.
- [Pivot](https://spw.quest/pivot?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You hold one line and want the lines one change away from it, grouped by the slot each turns. A turn that lands on a line a page already holds says which page, with a link to it. line: one line, 200 characters; past that it is cut and the page says so. In a browser, #turn-mode, #turn-body, #turn-subject, #turn-scope or #turn-projection scrolls to one slot; a fetch gets the whole page. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Find](https://spw.quest/specimens?q=recipe%5B*%5D): You want every line on spwashi.com with some shape: the same word through other lenses, the same lens on other words. q: slots to match, with * for any value. The page is about 250 KB raw (~34 KB gzipped): each shelf drawer previews up to 24 exemplars and search reads every line. Example: q = recipe[*].
- [Compare](https://spw.quest/specimens?a=h-capsule&b=h-induct_join): You hold two shelf lines and want the slots they share and the slot where they part. a, b: shelf ids, as Find prints them. The page is about 250 KB raw (~34 KB gzipped): each shelf drawer previews up to 24 exemplars and search reads every line. Example: a = h-capsule, b = h-induct_join.
- [Take apart](https://spw.quest/build?script=~door%5Bajar%5D%7Bhinge%7D): You hold a file, or a line among others, and want what a tool reads from it and each slot's alternatives from the file's own lines. script: up to 1800 characters in an address. line: which of its lines to take apart, counted from 1. Example: script = ~door[ajar]{hinge}.
- [Read a file](https://spw.quest/?example=record): You want a whole example of a kind of file (a log, a catalog record, a question with its probe) and what a tool reads from it. example: notebook, record, vocabulary, question, script, revision, persona, calibration, perspectives, loops, gradient, debate, syntax, headings, perform, numbers, outline, recurrence, laws, pantry, pipeline, review, records, surfaces, primitives, algorithms, role, levels, onboarding, cinema, checkin, decision, gathering, incident, critique, negotiation, charter, synthesis, table, lights, hearth or year. at: a name in the file, to land on its line. Example: example = record.
- [Check a line](https://spw.quest/read?step=act&line=~door): You are learning one mark and want a single line checked against that panel's rule. step: write, act, hold, name, point, ask or grow. line: up to 400 characters. Example: step = act, line = ~door.
- [At rest](https://spw.quest/physics?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a line drawn as bodies at rest, with the laws that placed them. line: one line. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Canvas](https://spw.quest/canvas?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a person to see a line laid out as a force-directed canvas on factshift.center. It draws with scripts, so a reader without them gets only its chrome: use Pivot to read the line. line: up to 400 characters, or s: a shelf id. Answers with a redirect to factshift.center. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.

## Reference

- [Marks and braces](https://spw.quest/#operators): each mark and brace pair, what it reads as, and what the runtime does with it.
- [Constructs](https://spw.quest/constructs): the shapes a line takes, each with a pressed example.
- [specimens.json](https://spw.quest/specimens.json): every specimen on the shelf, its line, where it comes from and its note, in one file.
- [Dated parser builds](https://spw.quest/parser/): the parser as a file to load on your own page.

## Optional

- [Initialize a repository](https://spw.quest/init): the recipe for mounting Spw Workbench, for an agent asked to set one up.
- [quest.json](https://spw.quest/quest.json): that recipe's facts as data.
- [Every example file](https://spw.quest/llms-full.txt): this index, then each file whole.

## Example files

lab-notebook.spw: A dated work log tagged by what happened: catalog something noticed, try an alternative, measure what changed, and land the fix.

    #>lab_notebook
    #:log #!components #!themes
    @chip: ~"./chip.spw"
    @matte: ~"./themes.spw#matte"

    ^"stream"{
     >>[2026-11-06 09:10] catalog — the chip, in three dialects on one screen: pill, ring, plain
     >>[2026-11-06 11:40] try — the matte theme on the chip: the ring holds its edge, the pill loses it
     >>[2026-11-06 14:05] measure — --shape-panel read 22 times in 11 files, with three fallbacks
     >>[2026-11-06 17:30] land — one inset for every panel on a phone
    }

chip.spw: A compact library card for one UI component: canonical name, aliases across teams, searchable subjects, and links to related specs.

    #>component_chip
    #:record #!component
    @broader: ~"./control.spw"
    @related: ~"./sigil.spw"
    @tried: ~"./experiment.spw"

    ^"record"{
      title = `chip`
      also_called = #[`pill`, `ring`, `plain`][reg=set]
      subjects = #[`handle`, `operator`, `touch target`][reg=set]
      provenance = `cataloged 2026-11-06 from three screens`
    }[reg=facet]

themes.spw: A shared glossary so designers and engineers use one canonical term instead of drifting between synonyms.

    #>theme_vocabulary
    #:vocabulary #!themes

    ^"matte"{
      use_for = #[`flat`, `chalk`][reg=set]
      scope = `a surface that takes no light; text sits on it at full contrast`
      broader = `metamaterial`
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"glass"{
      use_for = #[`frosted`, `liquid`][reg=set]
      scope = `a surface that lets what lies beneath show through, refracted`
      broader = `metamaterial`
    }[reg=facet]

experiment.spw: A testable UI question before opening a PR: state the hypothesis, predict the failing edge case, and name the screenshot or check that settles it.

    #>wonder_ring_on_glass
    @chip: ~"./chip.spw"
    @glass: ~"./themes.spw#glass"
    ?["Does the ring chip read on the glass theme at a phone's width?"]{
      ~#hypothesis: `a ring keeps its edge where a pill's fill washes out`
      ~#expect: `the ring holds 3:1 against the busiest panel; the pill does not`
      !probe{ "screenshot the chip row on glass at 390px and measure each edge's contrast" }
      $%[ring.reads, pill.reads, neither]
    }

session.spw: A short repeatable checklist in execution order, linking to the record it operates on.

    #>catalog_session
    #:script #!session
    @record: ~"./chip.spw#record"

    steps = path{~gather; *describe; ^classify; !shelve}
    gather = shelf[ui]{chip.card}<record>

change.spw: A three-part changelog or commit contract: what was broken in context, what changed, and how you verified it.

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ a panel body drew a second wall on a phone, and its text sat on the line }
      ![change]{ a body slot keeps no wall of its own below 45rem }
      *[verify]{ heading, body and first line share one edge on fourteen frames }
    }

archivist.spw: A working persona card for an assistant or teammate: tone, vantage point, core promise, and daily habit.

    #>archivist_persona
    #:persona #!library

    ^"persona"{
      voice = `plain, exact, fond of see-also`
      regards = `the component shelf from the reading room`
      affirms = `a record is a promise that a thing can be found again`
      stayed = `the habit of naming where each thing came from`
    }[reg=facet]

calibration.spw: A confidence check before and after studying or shipping: capture prediction errors early so estimates improve next round.

    #>calibration
    #:study #!metacognition

    ^"before"{
      predict = `I can say why recalling beats rereading`
      confidence = 0.7
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"after"{
      recalled = `two of the three reasons`
      confidence = 0.5
      next = `reread chapter 2 with a question written first`
    }[reg=facet]

    %confidence{before ~> after}

perspectives.spw: Four viewpoints on the same material — self, peer, future self, tutor — showing where each reader sees something different.

    #>four_readings
    #:reflection #!metacognition
    @measured: ~"./calibration.spw"

    me = student@ch2[sure]{recall}<quiz>
    peer = peer@ch2[unsure]{spacing}<ask>
    later = later@ch2[review]{kept}<exam>
    tutor = tutor@ch2[watch]{gap}<lesson>

    &ch2{recall, spacing, kept, gap}

loops.spw: Parallel team tracks that meet at explicit handoffs: spot the single dependency blocking another collaborator before work stalls.

    #>persona_loops
    #:board #!loops #!production
    @archivist: ~"./archivist.spw"

    reference = ~"./folios/release.spw"
    ahead = #[`the holds`, `the scans`][reg=set]
    loops = {
      archivist@scan{provenance},
      designer@scan{placement},
      editor@scan{caption}
    }
    each = path{~read; *note; ?ask; !hand_back}
    handoff = path{^gather; ?check; !release}
    relay = {archivist.provenance ~> editor.caption}

    ?["What must one loop hand another before it can start?"]{
      ~#expect: `only the caption waits, on provenance`
      !probe{ "list what each loop reads; what another loop writes goes in the handoff" }
    }

gradient.spw: A spectrum of concrete middle-ground options between two extremes, helping teams locate where they actually stand.

    #>gradient_space
    #:board #!gradient

    reference = ~"./plans/index.spw"
    from = archivist@plans{keep}
    to = designer@plans{reshape}
    gradient = #[
      `0.10 keep every line as written`,
      `0.40 keep the dates, rewrite the slices`,
      `0.70 keep the wonders, redraw the order`,
      `0.90 rebuild around the reader`
    ][reg=set]

    ?["Where on this gradient does each plan sit today?"]{
      ~#expect: `most sit near 0.40`
      !probe{ "read each plan's head line and name its place" }
    }

debate.spw: Three collaborators heard one word — cut — and walked away with three different plans. Putting every reading into the same slots exposes which constraint parted them, names quiet assumptions beside the lines, and logs each round toward repair.

    #>resolve_misunderstanding
    #:dialogue #!mediation
    @critique: ~"./review.spw#stance"

    topic = term[shared]{"hold the cut on Friday"}

    maya@[picture]{pacing, sound_lock}(friday)<cut>
    devon@[budget]{overtime, gear_return}(friday)<cut>
    priya@[story]{opening_scene, title_card}(tuesday)<cut>

    ^"assumptions"{
      ~#maya_expects(friday locks picture; mix runs next week)
      ~#devon_expects(friday ends stage rental and overtime)
      ~#priya_expects(tuesday trims narrative before sound mixes)
    }

    ^"rounds"{
      >>[2026-11-12 10:00] crux — Maya heard timing, Devon heard spend, Priya heard deletion
      >>[2026-11-12 10:15] reframe — separate priya@<trim> on Tuesday from maya@<lock> and devon@<wrap> on Friday
      >>[2026-11-12 10:30] settle — three named milestones replace the single overloaded word
    }

    ?["Can Tuesday narrative trim clear before Friday sound and wrap without overtime?"]{
      ~#expect: `naming trim and wrap separately turns one impasse into an ordered sequence`
      !probe{ "trace Tuesday trim ~> Thursday mix ~> Friday wrap and ask each speaker which blocker remains" }
    }

syntax.spw: Joins in pairs worth comparing: company and order (no order, then an order), reach and chain (~> goes toward, -> chains into), regard and subject (@ from where, & about what); a nest; and one line beside itself with one slot turned.

    #>syntax_stage
    #:showcase #!syntax
    @company: ~"./headings.spw#headings"

    company = {student, classmate, later}
    order = path{~read; *note; ?ask}
    reach = home ~> topics
    chain = draft -> page
    regard = student@indexing
    subject = &indexing{student, classmate}
    nest = shelf{chip{ring, pill}, card{lifted}}
    line = home[hook]{software.art}(atlas)<record>
    turned = home[live]{software.art}(atlas)<record>

headings.spw: Candidate taxonomy terms held together before committing one label across docs, navigation, or search.

    #>subject_headings
    #:showcase #!indexing #!library

    speaker = I
    wondered = indexing
    headings = {student, classmate, later}@indexing

    ?["Which heading would a catalog keep, and which stay in company?"]{
      ~#expect: `the three stay; the catalog's one term is a later choice`
      !probe{ "read the three names in the brace and say which one a shelf would authorize" }
    }

perform.spw: A live style directive: changing `theme` between glass, matte, and paper switches this workspace card's material on the spot.

    #>pattern_performance
    #:showcase #!pattern #!theme
    @line: ~"./syntax.spw#line"

    pattern = pivot
    performs = one.slot
    theme = glass
    line = home[hook]{software.art}<atlas>

    ?["When the pivot performs, which theme should the page take?"]{
      ~#expect: `glass, while one slot moves and the rest stays`
      !probe{ "change theme to matte and watch the field lose its shadow" }
    }

numbers.spw: A number written whole inside a measure's brackets, the way the workbench's number reader takes it: 400ms, 0.1%, 4/3, 1e6, a range 3.8..4.6%, and an uncertainty in its last digits, 412(18)ms. The body says what was measured and the scene when; a cost class rides in the concept; math Spw would misread stays in backticks. A percent's % still counts as a measure mark on this page.

    #>numbers
    #:showcase #!notation
    @metric: ~"./records.spw#metric"
    @cost: ~"./algorithms.spw#merge_sort"

    budget = ^checkout{ %p95[400ms] %errors[0.1%] =retries[3] }
    latency = %p95[412(18)ms]{checkout}(week)
    change = %p95{612ms ~> 412ms}(checkout)
    conversion = %rate[3.8..4.6%]{signup}(week)
    scale = %step[4/3]{type}
    rows = %count[1e6]{orders}
    cost = sort[merge]{runs}<O(n log n)>
    growth = `1 < log n < n < n log n < n^2 < 2^n`

    ?["Is checkout over its budget this week?"]{
      ~#expect: `not surely: 412(18)ms reaches down to 394ms, under 400ms`
      !probe{ "measure more requests until the uncertainty is under 12ms" }
    }

outline.spw: A course four levels deep: terms hold units, units hold weeks, weeks hold what is read and done.

    #>course_outline
    #:outline #!curriculum
    @session: ~"./session.spw"

    course = term{
      unit{
        week{read{chapter, margin}, do{drill, recall}},
        week{read{essay}, do{studio}}
      },
      unit{
        week{read{review}, do{retry}}
      }
    }

rain.spw: One word in four slots: rain as the subject, a part, a scene, and where a line goes.

    #>rain_ledger
    #:study #!identity
    @headings: ~"./headings.spw"

    morning = rain[light]{gutter, path}
    field = soil[wet]{rain, roots}
    song = chorus{verse, bridge}(rain)
    barrel = !water{roof ~> barrel}<rain>

kitchen.spw: Four neighbors under four laws: what lifts, what drifts, what stays, and what will not close.

    #>kitchen_laws
    #:showcase #!physics
    @perform: ~"./perform.spw"

    kitchen = {
      ^bread{flour, water},
      ~soup{beans, salt},
      =spice{cumin, clove},
      ?stock{bones, time}
    }

pantry.spw: A census of one shelf: sixteen things in company, read as a list and as a set of places.

    #>pantry_census
    #:record #!inventory

    pantry = shelf[full]{
      oats, rice, lentils, barley,
      salt, sugar, yeast, honey,
      vinegar, oil, cumin, clove,
      bay, thyme, sage, dill
    }

pipeline.spw: The common data-processing pass, in order: ground the units, fix the schema, keep valid rows, compute, join, group, sum, rank, index, show, and page on. Each step wears the mark that names its job.

    #>order_pipeline
    #:pipeline #!data
    @records: ~"./records.spw#schema"
    @review: ~"./review.spw"

    source = $orders[csv]{id, customer, qty, price}
    steps = path{
      .ground{utc, usd};
      =schema{qty, price};
      ?keep[valid]{qty, price};
      !map{total};
      &join{customers};
      ^group[by]{customer};
      %sum{total};
      *rank[desc]{total};
      #index{customer};
      @show[top]{ten};
      ~next{page}
    }
    run = {source ~> steps ~> report}

    ?["Which step must run before the sum?"]{
      ~#expect: `the keep, so a bad row never reaches %sum`
      !probe{ "move ?keep below %sum and read what the total now counts" }
    }

review.spw: One review point said three ways: by valence, from warm to blocking; by stance, from a question to a requirement, with a confidence; and by register, for a junior, a mid-level or a senior engineer.

    #>review_voice
    #:nuance #!review
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"

    point = keep{before ~> sum}

    ^"valence"{
      boon = `Good catch: no bad row reaches the sum.`
      bone = `The keep runs before the sum.`
      bane = `A bad row can still reach the sum.`
      bonk = `The total doubled after this merge.`
      honk = `This blocks the release.`
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"stance"{
      ask = ?point<curious>
      offer = ~point<suggestion>
      need = !point<blocking>
      credit = *point<kept>
      confidence = 0.8
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"register"{
      junior = explain[step]{why, how, try}
      mid = weigh[trade]{cost, option}
      senior = flag[risk]{scope, owner}
    }[reg=facet]

records.spw: The records a software team passes around, each in a line: a schema, a config, an API contract, a dependency graph, a test run, a metric, a diff, a ticket, a trace, and a dated log.

    #>engineering_records
    #:record #!engineering
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"

    schema = order{id, customer, qty, price}
    config = checkout[prod]{timeout, retries}
    contract = post[orders]{order ~> receipt}<api>
    deps = service{web ~> api, api ~> db}
    tests = suite[checkout]{pass, fail, skip}
    metric = latency[p95]{checkout}<week>
    diff = change[timeout]{ten ~> thirty}
    ticket = bug[open]{checkout, timeout}<t812>
    trace = request{web ~> api ~> db}<span>

    ^"log"{
     >>[2026-11-14 09:12] error — checkout timed out at 10s
     >>[2026-11-14 09:40] change — timeout raised to 30s
     >>[2026-11-14 10:05] measure — p95 back under 400ms
    }

surfaces.spw: The interactive surfaces of print and of the screen as two censuses, the hand each one asks for, and the print surface each screen surface grew from.

    #>publishing_surfaces
    #:census #!publishing
    @records: ~"./records.spw"

    print = book{
      cover, spine, endpaper, contents,
      spread, margin, footnote, caption,
      pull_quote, index, fold_out, insert
    }
    screen = page{
      link, button, menu, search,
      form, field, dialog, tab,
      scroll, carousel, comment, share,
      player, map, toast, tooltip
    }
    hands = {
      turn{spread, fold_out, insert},
      scan{contents, index, caption},
      tap{link, button, tab, share},
      type{search, field, comment},
      drag{scroll, carousel, map}
    }
    lineage = {
      contents ~> menu, index ~> search,
      footnote ~> tooltip, spread ~> scroll,
      margin ~> comment, insert ~> dialog
    }

primitives.spw: The values and structures most code is built from, each with what it does quickly and what that costs in O(): scalars, then lists, maps and sets, stacks and queues, heaps, trees and graphs.

    #>primitives
    #:census #!computing
    @algorithms: ~"./algorithms.spw#dedupe"

    scalars = {number, text, flag, none, time}
    array = list[indexed]{read, append}<O(1)>
    map = table[hashed]{put, get, has}<O(1)>
    set = table[unique]{add, has}<O(1)>
    stack = list[last_in]{push, pop}<O(1)>
    queue = list[first_in]{enqueue, dequeue}<O(1)>
    heap = tree[ordered]{push, pop_min}<O(log n)>
    tree = node[balanced]{value, children}<O(log n)>
    graph = node{value, edges}<O(V + E)>

    ?["Which structure would you reach for to dedupe a stream?"]{
      ~#expect: `a set, since has is O(1) where a list's is O(n)`
      !probe{ "count lookups per row with a list, then with a set" }
    }

algorithms.spw: Common algorithms as paths of marked steps, each with its cost class in the concept: search two ways, a sort beside its recurrence, three graph walks that differ only in what holds the frontier (a queue, a stack, a heap), an order of dependencies, a dedupe, a window, and a memo.

    #>algorithms
    #:study #!computing
    @primitives: ~"./primitives.spw"
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"

    linear_search = path{~scan{each}; ?compare{target}}<O(n)>
    binary_search = path{
      =range{low, high};
      ~halve{mid};
      ?compare{target};
      @return{index}
    }<O(log n)>
    merge_sort = path{~split{half}; *sort{each}; ^merge{runs}}<O(n log n)>
    recurrence = `T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n`
    bfs = path{=queue{start}; ~visit{edges}; #seen{node}}<O(V + E)>
    dfs = path{=stack{start}; ~visit{edges}; #seen{node}}<O(V + E)>
    dijkstra = path{=heap{start}; ~relax{edges}; #seen{node}}<O(E log V)>
    topo_sort = path{=queue{no_incoming}; ~remove{edges}; @emit{order}}<O(V + E)>
    dedupe = path{=set{seen}; ?has{row}; !add{row}}<O(n)>
    window = path{=edges{left, right}; ~slide; %sum{inside}}<O(n)>
    memo = path{?seen{subproblem}; !solve; #keep{answer}}<O(states)>

    ?["Which two lines differ in one word, and what does it change?"]{
      ~#expect: `bfs and dfs: a queue walks out by distance, a stack down by depth`
      !probe{ "walk the site's links from Home both ways and list the first five pages each reaches" }
    }

role.spw: One member's skills applied to a role: what they bring, the snippets they kept and where each came from, and what they will build first. A team can read every card and build from the snippets the cards point to.

    #>role_card
    #:role #!team
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"

    @surfaces: ~"./surfaces.spw"

    role = frontend[mid]{pages, forms, speed}<team>
    brings = skill{a11y, testing, design_handoff}
    kept = #[
      ~"./surfaces.spw#lineage",
      ~"./records.spw#metric",
      ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"
    ][reg=set]
    first = !build[form]{checkout ~> receipt}
    measure = %latency[p95]{before ~> after}

    ?["Which kept snippet does the first build lean on?"]{
      ~#expect: `the lineage, since a form grew from a printed one`
      !probe{ "build the form, then say which snippet you reread twice" }
    }

levels.spw: One ticket at four levels. The act and the problem stay the same on every line; what a junior, a mid-level, a senior and a staff engineer touch, where it lives, and how far ahead they plan each move one rung.

    #>levels
    #:compare #!engineering
    @ticket: ~"./records.spw#ticket"
    @onboarding: ~"./onboarding.spw"

    task = bug[open]{checkout, timeout}<t812>
    junior = !fix[timeout]{checkout}(function)<day>
    mid = !fix[timeout]{checkout, retries}(service)<week>
    senior = !fix[timeout]{retries, alert, budget}(system)<quarter>
    staff = !fix[timeout]{budget, owner, policy}(teams)<year>

    ?["What moves from one level to the next, and what stays?"]{
      ~#expect: `the act and the problem stay; the parts, the place and the horizon move`
      !probe{ "hold junior on the canvas, compare it with staff, and name each slot that moved" }
    }

onboarding.spw: Four paths through the team's files: what a junior, a mid-level, a senior and a staff engineer read first, change, and teach in their first week.

    #>team_onboarding
    #:plan #!onboarding
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"
    @review: ~"./review.spw#register"
    @records: ~"./records.spw"
    @surfaces: ~"./surfaces.spw"
    @levels: ~"./levels.spw"

    junior = path{~read{pipeline}; !change{one_step}; ?ask{review}}
    mid = path{^own{pipeline}; ~read{records}; !review{peer}}
    senior = path{*shape{surfaces}; =set{contract}; !teach{review}}
    staff = path{^align{teams}; *shape{records}; !write{levels}}
    week = {junior, mid, senior, staff} ~> demo

    ?["What can each of them change by Friday?"]{
      ~#expect: `a junior one step, a mid one record, a senior one contract, a staff one plan two teams share`
      !probe{ "each says in one line what they changed and where it shows" }
    }

incident.spw: Medium (23 lines). Blameless production P1 postmortem mixing exact SLA numbers, a dated timeline, root cause episode, and concrete follow-ups.

    #>inc_2026_11_12_checkout
    #:postmortem #!sre
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"
    @records: ~"./records.spw#ticket"

    impact = ^checkout{ %p95[412ms ~> 1840ms] %errors[0.1 ~> 4.8%] $window[19m] }
    responders = {
      @oncall[triage]{rollback, feature_flag}<mitigate>,
      @db_lead[diagnostics]{connection_pool, lock_wait}<root_cause>,
      @comms[status_page]{customer_notice, merchant_eta}<trust>
    }

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ a catalog sync deployed without jitter drained checkout read replicas }
      ![change]{ cap sync workers at 4 with exponential backoff and pool isolation }
      *[verify]{ soak test at 3x Tuesday peak holds p95 below 380ms }
    }

    ^"timeline"{
      >>[2026-11-12 14:02] alert — checkout p95 crossed 1200ms threshold in us-east
      >>[2026-11-12 14:11] isolate — paused catalog sync workers; connection wait dropped
      >>[2026-11-12 14:21] resolve — error rate returned to 0.08% across all shards
    }

vendor-sla.spw: Long & detailed (36 lines). Multi-team SaaS procurement and contract negotiation reconciling security, legal, and product constraints into concrete redlines.

    #>vendor_sla_negotiation
    #:contract #!procurement
    @incident: ~"./incident.spw"
    @gradient: ~"./gradient.spw"

    targets = ^sla{ %uptime[99.95%] %rto[4h] %rpo[15m] %p99_webhook[250ms] }
    non_negotiable = =security{
      soc2_type2,
      eu_residency,
      breach_notice[24h],
      key_rotation[90d]
    }

    stances = {
      @security[compliance]{audit_logs, subprocessor_notice}(pre_sign)<gate>,
      @legal[liability]{indemnity_cap, termination_notice}(msa)<redline>,
      @product[timeline]{sandbox_access, webhook_replay}(q4_launch)<value>
    }

    redlines = path{
      ~request[48h_breach_window ~> 24h_breach_window];
      =anchor[cap_2x_annual ~> cap_12m_fees];
      ^bundle[sso_saml, scim_provisioning]{included_at_tier}
    }

    ^"rounds"{
      >>[2026-11-04 11:00] draft — vendor standard MSA omitted subprocessor 30d objection right
      >>[2026-11-08 15:20] revise — vendor accepted 24h breach notice and EU cluster pinning
      >>[2026-11-13 10:15] counter — legal swapped unlimited cap for 2x fees plus data escrow
    }

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ launch slipped two weeks while security and vendor legal argued indemnity wording }
      ![change]{ separate operational security controls from liability cap using escrow trigger }
      *[verify]{ countersigned DPA plus passing sandbox webhook replay test before cutoff }
    }

field-study.spw: Long & detailed (38 lines). Research synthesis turning 14 recorded sessions into uncertainty bounds, opposing mental models, and an actionable product bet.

    #>checkout_accessibility_study
    #:research #!ux
    @calibration: ~"./calibration.spw"
    @incident: ~"./incident.spw"

    sample = ^cohort{
      %sessions[14]{screen_reader[5], low_vision[4], keyboard_only[3], voice[2]}
      %completion[0.64(0.12)]{coupon_flow}(mobile)
      %time_on_task[148(31)s ~> 62(14)s]{after_focus_fix}
    }

    mental_models = {
      @newcomer[visual]{expects_inline_error_by_button}(card_form)<feedback>,
      @screen_reader[sequential]{loses_focus_when_promo_drawer_remounts}(dom)<trap>,
      @keyboard_user[rapid]{needs_skip_to_pay_above_shipping_upsells}(tab_order)<speed>
    }

    tensions = &friction{
      speed_upsell ~ accessibility,
      animation ~ focus_stability,
      compact_summary ^ full_line_item_clarity
    }

    ^"bets"{
      *bet_one[inline_live_region]{announce coupon delta in aria_live instead of modal}<week>
      *bet_two[preserve_focus]{keep focus on toggle button across drawer open and close}<week>
      ~bet_three[one_page_summary]{collapse itemized taxes behind explicit disclosure}<quarter>
    }

    ^"sessions"{
      >>[2026-11-05 10:30] observe — VoiceOver jumped to footer when discount field cleared DOM
      >>[2026-11-09 14:15] prototype — stable DOM container cut promo abandonment in 4 of 5 trials
    }

    ?["Does fixing focus restoration raise VoiceOver completion past 0.85 without slowing sighted users?"]{
      ~#expect: `keeping one live node lifts screen-reader pass rate and trims median checkout by 18s`
      !probe{ "re-run the 5-task scripted benchmark with 8 assistive-tech testers on staging build" }
    }
